ECON 101.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 101.description: Introduction to consumer behaviour, producer theory, competitive market equilibrium, welfare economics, monopoly, oligopoly, and foundations of strategic interactions.

ECON 102.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 102.description: Elements of theory and of Canadian policy and institutions concerning the economics of growth and business cycles, employment, national income accounting, interest and exchange rates, money and banking, the balance of trade.

ECON 210.title: Microeconomic Policy
ECON 210.description: A survey of policy issues, such as regulation, taxation, environmental and resource policy, health care, education and income distribution. May not be taken for credit by students with fourth-year standing.
ECON 210.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 211.title: Macroeconomic Policy
ECON 211.description: A survey of policy issues, such as the costs of inflation and unemployment, monetary and fiscal policy, the effects of government debt and exchange rate policy. May not be taken for credit by students with fourth-year standing.
ECON 211.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 221.title: Introduction to Strategic Thinking
ECON 221.description: How individuals and businesses interact in strategic situations with applications in a wide range of topics which may include economics, business, politics, law and biology. Focus on developing intuition. May not be taken for credit by 1) students with fourth-year standing in ECON or the B.I.E., or 2) students that have taken ECON 421 or MATH 344.

ECON 226.title: Making Sense of Economic Data
ECON 226.description: Techniques of introductory empirical economics with an emphasis on foundational econometric methods and answering economic questions using real-world data. Students will be expected to undertake applied work using a statistical programming tool. May not be taken for credit by students with fourth-year standing in ECON, or students already having credit for ECON 325, ECON 327, COMM 191, STAT 200, STAT 241, STAT 251.
ECON 226.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of ECON 101, ECON 310, ECON 102 or (b) ECON 311

ECON 227.title: Data in Economics
ECON 227.description: Application-driven introduction to the analysis of economic data. Descriptive analysis, causality, experimental and observational data, hypothesis testing. Restricted to BIE students.

ECON 234.title: Wealth and Poverty of Nations
ECON 234.description: Historical approaches to long-run economic growth; international comparisons of income growth and inequality; colonialism; evolution of world capital markets; human migrations; rise of world trading empires; instability in the international economy. May not be taken for credit by students with fourth-year standing in Bachelor of International Economics or any of the following Economics programs offered by VSE: Majors, Minors, Combined Majors, Honours.
ECON 234.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 241.title: Introduction to Global Development
ECON 241.description: Economic approaches to long-run global development, international trade, growth, and globalization. Topics include the economics of trade policy, political economy, migration, the environment, foreign investment, and culture in a global context. Students may only receive credit for ECON_V 241 and ECON_V 255 or ECON_V 234 with permission of the instructor.
ECON 241.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311

ECON 255.title: Understanding Globalization
ECON 255.description: Social and economic implications for both rich and poor countries of lowered barriers to the international flows of information, capital, labour and goods. May not be taken for credit by students with fourth-year standing in Bachelor of International Economics or any of the following Economics programs offered by VSE: Majors, Minors, Combined Majors, Honours.
ECON 255.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 301.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Analysis I
ECON 301.description: Consumer behaviour, producer theory, competitive market equilibrium, welfare economics, uncertainty, monopoly and oligopoly.
ECON 301.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100, MATH_O 116 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_V 103

ECON 302.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis I
ECON 302.description: Income and employment theory, monetary theory, the open economy, economic fluctuations and growth.
ECON 302.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100, MATH_O 116 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

ECON 303.title: Intermediate Microeconomics II
ECON 303.description: Risk and uncertainty, some concepts in game theory, adverse selection, moral hazard, bargaining, auctions.
ECON 303.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 304.title: Honours Intermediate Microeconomic Analysis I
ECON 304.description: Consumer behaviour, uncertainty, producer theory, monopoly, oligopoly, and equilibrium analysis.

ECON 304.prerequisiteText: All of (i) a score of 68% or higher in one of ECON 101, ECON 310; (ii) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184; and (iii) completion of one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121

ECON 305.title: Honours Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis I
ECON 305.description: Income and employment theory, monetary theory, the open economy, economic fluctuations and growth.

children.raw: A score of 68% or higher in

a score of 68% or higher in
a score of 68% or higher in

ECON 305.prerequisiteText: A score of 68% or higher in one of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and a score of 68% or higher in one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102 and a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100 and a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

ECON 306.title: Honours Intermediate Microeconomics II
ECON 306.description: Microeconomic Theory with computational applications. Topics may include risk and uncertainty, information economics, game theory, bargaining, auctions. Knowledge of python and Julia is useful but not required.

children.raw: A score of 68% or higher in

ECON 306.prerequisiteText: A score of 68% or higher in ECON 304. Permission of the School is also acceptable

ECON 307.title: Honours Intermediate Macroeconomics II
ECON 307.description: Theories of economic growth and the business cycle. Intended primarily for prospective honours and other qualified students.

children.raw: A score of 68% or higher in

ECON 307.prerequisiteText: A score of 68% or higher in ECON 305. Or permission of the School

ECON 309.title: Intermediate Open Economy Macroeconomics
ECON 309.description: The aggregate economy with emphasis on macroeconomic policy and international economic growth, money and inflation, unemployment, business cycles, and macroeconomic stabilization policy under fixed and flexible exchange rates. Registration restricted to students in the Bachelor of International Economics Program.
ECON 309.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

ECON 310.title: Principles of Microeconomics with Calculus
ECON 310.description: Introduction to consumer behaviour, producer theory, competitive market equilibrium, welfare economics, monopoly, oligopoly, and strategic interactions with applications using differential calculus. The scope of this course is approximately the same as that of ECON_V 101.

ECON 311.title: Principles of Macroeconomics with Calculus
ECON 311.description: Elements of theory and of Canadian policy and institutions concerning the economics of growth, business cycles, employment, national income accounting, interest, exchange rates, money, banking, and trade, with applications using differential calculus. The scope of this course is approximately the same as that of ECON_V 102.

ECON 315.title: Intermediate Microeconomics I
ECON 315.description: Consumer behaviour, producer theory, exchange, monopoly, oligopoly, externalities, public goods, general equilibrium and welfare economics. Registration restricted to students in the Bachelor of International Economics Program.
ECON 315.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

ECON 316.title: Intermediate Microeconomics II
ECON 316.description: Advanced topics in intermediate microeconomics: risk and uncertainty, some concepts in game theory, adverse selection, moral hazard, bargaining, auctions. Registration restricted to students in the Bachelor of International Economics Program.

ECON 317.title: Poverty and Inequality
ECON 317.description: Economic inequality in Canada and other countries; measurement and causes. Inequality in the distribution of wealth; redistribution of income and wealth; notions of distributive justice.
ECON 317.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102

ECON 318.title: History and Philosophy of Economics from Aristotle to Adam Smith
ECON 318.description: The development of economic thought from Aristotle to Adam Smith, focusing on the conceptual foundations of economics, particularly the problems of value, distribution, and economic growth.

ECON 319.title: History and Philosophy of Economics from Ricardo to Keynes
ECON 319.description: The development of economic thought from David Ricardo up to the present including such figures as Malthus, Mill, Jevons, and Keynes, focusing on the conceptual foundations of economics, particularly the problems of value, distribution and growth.
ECON 319.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102

ECON 320.title: Introduction to Mathematical Economics
ECON 320.description: Application of single and multivariable calculus to economics. Includes comparative static analysis of household and firm behaviour as well as simple dynamic models. ECON 320 cannot be counted as satisfying ECON requirements for the Combined Major in Economics/Mathematics.
ECON 320.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311 and one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121

ECON 323.title: Quantitative Economic Modelling with Data Science Applications
ECON 323.description: Computational tools used in modern economics. Including application of data science in economics; visualization and manipulation of economic data; solving and simulating dynamic economic models. One course in second-year linear algebra such as MATH 221 or MATH 223 is strongly recommended, but not required.
ECON 323.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121

ECON 325.title: Introduction to Econometrics I
ECON 325.description: Essentials of probability and statistics for applied work in economics. Topics include fundamentals of probability and statistical inference including estimation and hypothesis testing, and simple linear regression models.
ECON 325.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100, MATH_O 116 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

ECON 326.title: Introduction to Econometrics II
ECON 326.description: Methods of empirical economic research. Topics include multiple linear regression models, with a focus on regression diagnostics, prediction, statistical inference, and interpretations. Students will be required to learn to apply empirical methods using a statistical programming tool.
ECON 326.prerequisiteText: All of ECON_V 101 or ECON_O 101, ECON_V 102 or ECON_O 102; one of ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, COMM_V 191, STAT_V 200, STAT_V 241, STAT_V 251, LFS_V 252, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 124, STAT_O 230

ECON 327.title: Introduction to Empirical Methods
ECON 327.description: Basic tools for the statistical analysis of economic data. Registration restricted to students in the Bachelor of International Economics Program.
ECON 327.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311; and one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184; and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121

ECON 328.title: Methods of Empirical Research
ECON 328.description: Empirical tools used in applied research, with emphasis on the linear regression model. Registration restricted to students in the Bachelor of International Economics program.

ECON 333.title: Economic History of Europe from the Paleolithic to the Industrial Revolution
ECON 333.description: The conditions and causes of long run growth from nomadism to agriculture to industrialized states, including institutions, geography, culture, colonialism, and slave trades. Determinants of the Neolithic, consumer and industrial revolutions, demographic transition and first era of globalization.
ECON 333.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102

ECON 334.title: Economic History of Modern Europe
ECON 334.description: Background, causes and effects of economic change in Europe from the 18th century to recent times. Evolution of social and economic institutions; analysis of growth, structural change, the distribution of income, and the spread of industrialization.
ECON 334.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 335.title: Fertility, Families and Human Migration
ECON 335.description: Traditional fertility and mortality patterns, demographic transition, catastrophes, well-being and nutrition, international and internal migration, epidemics and growth spurts.
ECON 335.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 336.title: Economic History of Canada
ECON 336.description: The growth of the Canadian economy in relation to development of natural resources, changing markets, industrialism, communications, and technology.

ECON 337.title: Economic History of the United States
ECON 337.description: The growth of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present: British colonialism, development of slave-based agriculture, the western expansion, the 'American system' of manufacturing, cyclical instability and depression, and the distribution of income.
ECON 337.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 339.title: Economics of Technological Change
ECON 339.description: Application of economic analysis to technological change; the impact of technological change on the growth and distribution of income; economic influences on the invention and diffusion of technology; the interaction between technology, work, skills, and education; public policy toward technological change.
ECON 339.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 345.title: Money and Banking
ECON 345.description: Financial markets and financial institutions in theory and practice; structure and development of the Canadian financial system; development and theory of the regulation of the financial system; process of monetary control; theory and history of central banking and monetary policy.
ECON 345.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102

ECON 350.title: Public Finance Policy Topics
ECON 350.description: Examination of two or three selected policy problems from areas of taxation, income security, and public expenditures. Topics to be selected each year from areas of current or recent policy debate. Examples include public pension policy, privatization and public services, income tax or sales tax reform, federal-provincial cost sharing programs, tax incentives versus direct expenditures, welfare reform.
ECON 350.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 351.title: Sex and Gender in the Economy
ECON 351.description: Application of economic analysis to marriage, fertility and health, gender inequality in labour markets and unpaid caregiving; the application of sex and gender-based policy analysis to topics related to employment, and technological and social change in current and historical perspectives.
ECON 351.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 355.title: Introduction to International Trade
ECON 355.description: The determinants of trade patterns, trade policy, tariff and non-tariff barriers to trade, political economy of protectionism, bilateral and multilateral trade disputes, trade liberalization, trade and development.
ECON 355.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 356.title: Introduction to International Finance
ECON 356.description: Exchange rate policy regimes; international financial organizations; the interaction between monetary policy and exchange rate regimes; financial crises.
ECON 356.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102

ECON 360.title: Labour Economics
ECON 360.description: A study of the Canadian labour market. Labour supply, the allocation of the time among work and non-market activity, participation in the labour force, education and training. The demand for labour. The determination of wages and employment. The effect of unions on wages and employment. The wage structure, wage differentials by occupation, industry, race and sex. Unemployment.

ECON 364.title: The Economics of Sustainable Development: Communities, Markets and Technology
ECON 364.description: Research and seminars on topics of concern to economists and communities located locally and internationally. Environmental sustainability, sustainable livelihoods, development effectiveness, institutions, agency, ethics, and well-being. Theoretical approaches, case studies, and community-based learning. Restricted to BA students with at least 3rd year standing and BIE students with at least 2nd year standing. Students are expected to have completed at least 9 ECON credits prior to registration.
ECON 364.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 365.title: Topics in Canadian Industrial Organization and Regulation Policy
ECON 365.description: Current topics in industrial organization and regulation with emphasis on Canadian federal and provincial policy. The content will differ from year to year. Possible subjects include the regulation of transportation and communications, environmental regulation, marketing boards and other forms of agricultural regulation, competition and anti-combines policy, industrial organization and trade policy, and issues in consumer protection.
ECON 365.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 367.title: Economic Analysis of Law
ECON 367.description: The economics of market failure, equity and efficiency. Property rights, the economics of accident and contract law, economic theories of law enforcement.
ECON 367.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 370.title: Benefit-Cost Analysis and the Economics of Project Evaluation
ECON 370.description: Techniques and problems in benefit-cost analysis of public projects. Examination of alternative approaches to public decision-making such as cost-effectiveness analysis and multiple-objective frameworks. Case studies of projects in the areas of natural resources, the environment, human resources, public services, and transportation.

ECON 371.title: Economics of the Environment
ECON 371.description: Economic analysis applied to various environmental issues, including sustainable development, quality of life, and environmental impacts of specific industrial and consumption activities. The design and implementation of government policies. Global environmental effects of human economic activity.

ECON 374.title: Land Economics
ECON 374.description: Economic analysis applied to problems of land use. Rent theory. Land valuation. Land conservation. Techniques for assessing economic efficiency of land use. Effects of institutions and public policies on land use.

ECON 384.title: Economic Analysis of Health Services
ECON 384.description: Microeconomic theory of resource allocation with emphasis on the applications of optimizing models of health service markets. Analysis of Canadian problems in health service supply. Models of the consumer/patient, the physician/entrepreneur, the not-for-profit hospital/firm, and the third-party regulatory and payment agency.
ECON 384.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 390.title: Introduction to Economic Research
ECON 390.description: Selected topics in economic research. Application of research methods to economic data.
ECON 390.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310, ECON_O 101 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 102 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100

ECON 392.title: Topics in Economics
ECON 392.description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website ( for more information.
ECON 392.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 101, ECON 310 and one of ECON 102, ECON 311

ECON 398.title: Introduction to Causal Methods
ECON 398.description: Theory and practice of the analytical application of economics. Causality, causal modeling, empirical analysis, and the use of theoretical models in policy evaluation and other practical applications.
ECON 398.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 102, ECON_V 310, ECON_V 311, ECON_O 101, ECON_O 102 and one of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 201, STAT_V 241, STAT_V 251, COMM_V 191, FRST_V 231, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 124, STAT_O 230; or (b) one of ECON_V 226, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 326, ECON_V 327; or (c) permission of the instructor

ECON 406.title: Topics in Microeconomics
ECON 406.description: Selected topics in advanced microeconomic analysis.
ECON 406.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 303, ECON 306, ECON 316

ECON 407.title: Topics in Macroeconomics
ECON 407.description: Selected topics in advanced macroeconomic analysis.
ECON 407.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 302, ECON 305, ECON 309

ECON 408.title: Computational Methods in Macroeconomics
ECON 408.description: Computational tools and algorithms used in macroeconomics and financial economics including applications to unemployment, inequality, asset pricing, and economic growth.
ECON 408.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315 and one of ECON 323, CPSC 103, CPSC 107, CPSC 110, CPSC 301, MATH 210, COMM 337, PHYS 210, EOSC 211, APSC 160 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

ECON 420.title: Optimization and Economic Theory
ECON 420.description: An introduction to static and dynamic optimization methods with economic applications.
ECON 420.prerequisiteText: MATH 200 and one of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 421.title: Introduction to Game Theory and Applications
ECON 421.description: Principles of rational behaviour in strategic situations and various notions of equilibrium useful in predicting outcomes. Applications from economics, business, politics, law and biology.
ECON 421.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 422.title: Mathematics for Economists
ECON 422.description: Provides the required preparation in mathematics for the study of graduate economic theory. Solving systems of simultaneous equations; unconstrained and constrained maxima; elementary theory of difference and differential equations. Restricted to students taking graduate economic theory courses.

ECON 425.title: Advanced Econometrics
ECON 425.description: The study and analysis of advanced econometric models. Topics may include statistical inference on various models with nonlinearity and endogeneity, such as models with instrumental variables, discrete-choice models, panel regression models, models of causal inference, and machine learning methods.
ECON 425.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 326, ECON 328, STAT 306, LFS 252

ECON 426.title: Econometric Analysis
ECON 426.description: Further topics in econometrics including such areas as nonlinear estimation, distributed lag models, time-series analysis, time-varying parameters, multivariate analysis, simulation and forecasting models, Monte Carlo experiments, duration models, large econometric models, Bayesian statistics, asymptotic theory, and ergodic theory.

ECON 441.title: The Process of Economic Development
ECON 441.description: Industrialization of an agrarian economy; how the West grew rich; history of Japanese development; technical progress and growth; evolution of the patterns of income distribution; role of international trade in development; environment and development.
ECON 441.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 442.title: Issues in Economic Development
ECON 442.description: Divergence in the world economy, poverty, consequences of initial inequality, institutions, the impact of history, recent developmental experience--some case studies, labour and credit markets, the trickle down process.
ECON 442.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 447.title: Monetary Theory
ECON 447.description: Theoretical analysis of economies that use money; the emergence of money; the roles of money in the economy; models of money demand; the optimal quantity of money seignorage and inflation; monetary policy and macroeconomic stability; monetary policy in an open economy.
ECON 447.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 302, ECON 305, ECON 309

ECON 450.title: Economics of Taxation
ECON 450.description: Economic analysis of taxation. Equity, efficiency, and incidence of government revenue sources such as personal and corporate income taxes, sales taxes, property taxes, payroll taxes, and environmental taxes.
ECON 450.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 302, ECON 305, ECON 309

ECON 451.title: Economics of Public Expenditures
ECON 451.description: The role of government in the economy; efficiency and economic justice. Theory of public goods; applications to topics such as education, medical care and social services. Pricing and investment rules for public enterprises.
ECON 451.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 302, ECON 305, ECON 309

ECON 455.title: International Trade
ECON 455.description: International trade theory and policy in general equilibrium; relative costs, factor proportions, imperfect competition and the pattern of trade; efficiency and distribution.
ECON 455.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 456.title: International Macroeconomics and Finance
ECON 456.description: Balance of payments; market for foreign exchange; mechanism for adjusting the balance of payments; internal vs. external stability; current problems and issues.

ECON 457.title: Seminar in International Economic Relations
ECON 457.description: Selected topics focusing upon various issues arising in international economic relations. Open only to fourth-year students in the Major program in International Relations. Credit shall not count towards 400-level ECON courses for economics majors, combined majors, honours, and the B.I.E.
ECON 457.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 310 and one of ECON_V 102, ECON_V 311

ECON 460.title: Economics of Labour Markets
ECON 460.description: The theory of labour supply and demand for individuals, households, and firms. Policy implications for Canadian taxation and benefit programs. Employee selection, hiring and promotion.
ECON 460.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 302, ECON 305, ECON 309

ECON 465.title: Market Structure
ECON 465.description: Market structure and social welfare, theory of price discrimination, equilibrium in oligopolistic markets, entry and exit decisions, product differentiation and spatial models, theories of hierarchical organization, agency problem in the modern corporation, vertical integration and control, market structure and technical progress.
ECON 465.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 466.title: The Economics of Government Regulation of Business
ECON 466.description: Normative and positive theories of government regulation of business. Topics include natural monopoly, socially optimal monopoly pricing, regulation of multi-firm industries, competition policy. Selected empirical studies.
ECON 466.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 467.title: Economics of Crime and Policing
ECON 467.description: The application of methods and theory to topics related to the criminal justice system with a specific focus on the role of policy in reducing crime rates, punitiveness and systemic inequality.
ECON 467.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295 and one of ECON 326, ECON 328, STAT 306, LFS 252

ECON 471.title: Economics of Nonrenewable Resources
ECON 471.description: Application of economic analysis to the management of nonrenewable natural resources. Emphasis is placed on the economics of alternative energy sources. Other topics include mineral economics, criteria for the optimal use of resources, and measurement of resources.
ECON 471.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 472.title: Economics of Renewable Resources
ECON 472.description: Application of economic analysis to the management of renewable resources. Special attention is given to criteria for the optimal use of depleting resources such as forests and water. Other topics include public policy with regard to environmental quality, conservation, and outdoor recreation.
ECON 472.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 473.title: Economics of Climate Change
ECON 473.description: The impact of climate change as examined through economic thinking and research. Social and economic outcomes, social cost of carbon, policies to mitigate or adapt to climate change, and climate justice.
ECON 473.prerequisiteText: One of ECON_V 301, ECON_V 304, ECON_V 315, COMM_V 295 or FRST_V 318; and one of ECON_V 326, ECON_V 328, STAT_V 306, or FRE_V 326

ECON 482.title: The Economic Consequences of Religion
ECON 482.description: Analysis of the economic aspects of religious behaviour, the structure of religious organizations, the effects of competition in the religious marketplace, the economic benefits of religion, and some of the ill-effects of religion (such as religious strife and terrorism).
ECON 482.prerequisiteText: One of ECON 301, ECON 304, ECON 315, COMM 295

ECON 485.title: Political Economy
